events.text:
Confirmed in the installer: what ships is `.agents/`, the entry file and the host stub, never `docs/` or the local file, and a new tree's queue arrives with the arrival text alone.

| 🪢 Tangle · [q-0037.0013](docs/questions/q-0037.0013-how-does-each-turn-know-its-next-step-and-each-session-where-to-resume.md) · [q-0037.0012.0009](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0009-how-is-an-amendment-to-an-instruction-tested-before-it-lands-against-which-cases-chosen-how-run-with-no-instruction-the-standing-one-and-the-new-one.md) · — · — |
|---|

| 📍 **q-0037.0013** · How does each turn know its next step, and each session where to resume? |
|---|

**On the shift.** I think it is right, and it says what the order already does. *Work better* reads two ways: better for the recipients who use the harness, or better at building itself. The queue has picked the second every time it had to choose: the whole coherence chain stands ahead of the releases chain and the arrival work, which are the recipients' needs, and the reason given is that the pacer waits for skills to become mechanisms. *Develop itself better* names that choice instead of leaving it to be inferred from the first clause, *the harness is self-building*. The compounding is the point: a slice that gives the next slice a check or a rule makes every later slice cheaper and safer to land, and the order is a bet on that compounding (💡 [*How this queue is ordered*](docs/tickets/README.md:16)).

One thing the reworded rule still does not say, and need not: when a recipient's need outranks the compounding. The queue already handles that by your hand, dated, as with `.0175` pulled forward on 2026-10-14. A clause for it would be a rule the work would not miss (💡 [*Occam*](AGENTS.md:30)).

The text as it would stand, inside the straw dog that already wraps the paragraph:

✏️ **Proposed change — [docs/tickets/README.md](docs/tickets/README.md) · How this queue is ordered**

> **How this queue is ordered** *(the user, 2026-09-07; reworded 2026-10-20)*: the harness is self-building, so the governing consideration is which slice hands the next one a tool that makes the harness develop itself better — not dependency order alone, and not size. A slice that only describes something ranks below one that gives the next slice a script, a check or a rule it can lean on. The pacer owns this once it exists ([01-0020](docs/tickets/01-0020-each-turn-knows-its-next-step.md)); until then it is stated here and applied by hand.

Ordering what gets built next is 🛠️ development=a product slice, above the dial, so this is yours to decide; the text lands on your yes (💡 [*Above it, it settles nothing*](AGENTS.md:221)).

**On where it lives.** Yes, it is this tree's own and reaches no recipient. The paragraph stands in this repository's queue under `docs/`, the instance half, which is this project's like any other project's (💡 [*L1*](AGENTS.md:255)). The installer ships every file under the core directory, the entry file and the host stub, and nothing of `docs/` or the local file; a tree that has just received core gets a queue holding only *the project's own setup, then its first align*. Two things follow:

- The rule is the right kind of thing for this tree: a project-specific answer, consistent with the harness being its own recipient.
- When the pacer exists and ordering becomes a mechanism's, the mechanism will carry the generic method and each project its own consideration, this one's being self-development. Where a project's consideration lives then, the queue or its local file, is open under q-0037.0013, which the straw dog on the paragraph already binds.

| ⚖️ Decisions |
|---|
| The rewording above, landing in the queue on your yes |
| Take [01-0010.0175](docs/tickets/01-0010.0175-arrival-describes-what-it-finds.md) next, its `/plan` |
| [q-0037.0012.0003](docs/questions/q-0037.0012.0003-what-does-an-entry-contract-version-cover.md) waits at `/align`, as the queue has held since 2026-10-08 |
